A1.justification: Both 29-page PDFs describe the same work, Temporal Straightening for Latent Planning. The main text and Appendices A–F, including figures, tables, equations and proofs, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original planning simulations on Wall, PointMaze and PushT, including success rates, ablations, long-horizon experiments and Teleported-PointMaze case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and reports revised success rates in Tables 1 and 5 and an additional PushT MPC curve in Figure 8d.

M1.justification: The JEPA architecture, curvature objective, aggregation head and GD/MPC planning procedures remain unchanged. Updated diagrams illustrate stop-gradient operations already specified in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions cover Wall, PointMaze-UMaze, PointMaze-Medium, PushT, the same long-horizon settings and Teleported-PointMaze. No dataset, task or environment coverage is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the DINO-WM/DINOv2 baselines, encoder controls without straightening, GD/CEM comparisons, and smoothness and temporal-contrastive comparators. Revised scores do not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Table 3 revises the stated learning rate for regularized global Projector/ResNet encoders from the general 1e-5 default to 1e-6. The 1e-6 exception for training without straightening already existed. This establishes a limited reported-setting revision, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figure 8d adds a PushT MPC success-versus-steps curve for straightening strength lambda = 0.01, extending the existing sensitivity analysis. The other ablations, long-horizon analyses, visualizations and teleportation case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly discloses two held-out validation seeds for selecting global-feature regularization strength. Test results still use mean ± standard deviation over three evaluation-data seeds; an increase in test runs or a new uncertainty-estimation procedure is not established.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises global-feature results: straightened global ResNet's PushT open-loop/MPC rates change from 19.33%/48.67% to 58.67%/83.33%, alongside revised reported settings. Table 5 revises four DINOv2 patch GD baseline rates, including Wall from 73.33% to 52.67%, to agree with Table 1. Figure 8d also adds lambda = 0.01 results. These materially revise the empirical comparisons.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same linear-dynamics assumptions, conditioning bounds, cosine-proxy proposition and proofs. Figure-caption notation corrections do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about temporal straightening, geodesic-distance alignment, planning conditioning and improved goal-reaching performance.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 narrows the statement about gains exceeding 10% from 'almost all setups' to 'across many setups.' Mechanism explanations and long-horizon/asymmetric-dynamics limitations remain unchanged; the quasimetric discussion gains citations rather than a new limitation.

D1.justification: Table 1 newly documents MPC-based validation selection of global-feature regularization strengths and the selected coefficients. Table 3 distinguishes global and spatial learning rates. Appendix B.3 identifies PushT as the runtime benchmark, and Table 5 explicitly specifies CEM's 200 samples and 10 iterations. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Wang and Isola (2022) and cites it alongside the already included Wang et al. (2023) for quasimetric planning costs. Duplicate SOLAR bibliography entries are consolidated without removing a distinct cited work. Broader research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local edits correct captions, replace 'test samples' with 'test episodes,' shorten results paragraphs and clean up bibliography entries. Section order, appendix organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 13 revise arrows and explicitly mark stop-gradient operations. Figure 8d adds a curve, uncertainty band and legend entry. Table 1 gains regularization annotations, and Table 3 gains a separate global-feature row, with limited accompanying layout shifts.

improvement.justification: V3 resolves conflicting GD baseline values between Tables 1 and 5 and improves reproducibility through clearer regularization-selection and experimental-setting documentation. It also qualifies one broad performance generalization and clarifies diagrams. These are limited, supported quality gains; higher revised scores under partly changed settings do not themselves establish improvement.
